The Dunghutti, also spelt Dainggatti or Djangadi, are an Aboriginal people of the Macleay Valley on the mid north coast of New South Wales, around present day Kempsey.

Their country runs from the coast up the Macleay River into the gorges of the New England tableland. Neighbours were the Gumbaynggirr to the north, the Birpai to the south and the Anaiwan on the tableland.

Cedar cutters came up the Macleay in the 1830s, followed by farmers. In the 1900s many Dunghutti people lived on reserves and missions around Kempsey, and many still live in the valley today. The map shows them from 1600 to 1800. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
sum: The Dunghutti, also spelt Dainggatti or Djangadi, are an Aboriginal people of the Macleay Valley on the mid north coast of New South Wales, around present day Kempsey.
